correctness.rationale: A longest chain above a nonterminal world ends at an accessible terminal world by transitivity. Thus Box Diamond p and Diamond Box p have complementary, valuation-independent values. The two Boolean inputs used for a witness to non-self-duality are exactly a and its complement. Conversely, induct on formula size using the scopes of the outermost modal subformulas as proper subformulas. Adjoining a new root with arrows to every world in disjoint satisfying/refuting witness components preserves transitivity and irreflexivity, and adds no outgoing edges to any old world. At the new root boxes in the Boolean skeleton are false and diamonds true; at an isolated terminal world they have the opposite values. Complementing root assignments and applying self-duality through the skeleton proves contingency. Finite-frame completeness gives the asserted GL equivalences. At the root of a two-world chain, all-true and all-false valuations make each modal-free or depth-one input of the conjunction/disjunction skeleton uniform, proving the depth obstruction. The packaged checker was read, not executed; the argument is analytic and does not rely on its bounded enumeration.

evidence: A non-self-dual witness gives a binary minor g with equal values at (0,1) and (1,0). If its diagonal is constant, the clone already has a constant; if its diagonal is negation, g(p,not p) gives a constant; otherwise g is AND or OR. Thus Example 4.11 and its dual already imply the existence half at the clone level.
Neither this implication nor the general Type C bounds prove the converse, the stronger contingency assertion, or the depth lower bounds.

value.rationale: This gives a complete clone criterion for a natural expressibility boundary in GL, with a uniform exclusion for unbounded modal nesting. The two-world depth obstruction identifies the first depth at which both modalities can increase this particular expressive power, rather than merely offering another syntax for a previously known example.
